title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` non-negative integers. The **XOR total** of a subset is the bitwise XOR of all of its elements; the empty subset has XOR total `0`.

Consider every subset of `nums`, where subsets are distinguished by the positions they pick (so equal values at different positions give different subsets, and there are exactly `2^n` subsets). Compute the sum of the XOR totals of all these subsets.

The sum can be extremely large, so print it modulo `1000000007`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the sum of all subset XOR totals modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The eight subsets have XOR totals 0, 2, 4, 8, 6, 10, 12 and 14, which add up to 56.
The subsets {}, {5}, {5}, {5, 5} have XOR totals 0, 5, 5 and 0, so the sum is 10. The two single-element subsets count separately because they use different positions.
The subsets are {} and {7}, with XOR totals 0 and 7.

hints: With n up to 10^5 you cannot enumerate the 2^n subsets. Look at one bit position at a time.
Fix a bit. If no element has that bit set, it never contributes. If at least one element has it, exactly half of all subsets (2^(n-1) of them) have that bit set in their XOR total.
So every bit that appears in at least one element contributes `bit * 2^(n-1)`. Combine these with a single bitwise OR of all elements, and use fast modular exponentiation.
